description:
The Bastion Mesh is a military-grade subdermal armor system consisting of interlocking boron-carbide ceramic hexagonal tiles bonded to a titanium-weave backing, surgically implanted beneath the dermis across the torso, upper arms, and thighs in a full-coverage configuration. Sections over major joints and the skull use flexible articulated tile arrays to preserve movement while maintaining protection; the system is rated to stop most handgun rounds outright and significantly reduce penetration from rifle calibers. Chrome-finished titanium frame sections are intentionally left visible at the shoulders, sternum, and forearms — a deliberate ARCTURUS design choice signaling military provenance and deterrence.

Bastion is restricted to active and veteran military, licensed contractors, and certain law enforcement units — civilian possession is a serious offense. On the black market it commands extraordinary prices, and the visible chrome plating sections make it nearly impossible to conceal, meaning users are making a deliberate statement about their threat level. Former soldiers who kept their Bastion implants after discharge exist in a legal grey zone that the GMPD actively monitors; some operate as high-end security contractors, others as heavily-armored criminals.

rejection_risk: Moderate — extensive surface area increases infection risk; titanium weave requires full osseointegration across multiple anchor zones; rejection events are rare but catastrophic
maintenance: Annual tile integrity scan; cracked tiles require surgical replacement; titanium frame polishing is optional but culturally common among users
